title: The tech says apply
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wood mentions the application at the print shop, casually, as a thing he isn't doing. The tech doesn't look up. 'I'll run the portfolio free. Once.' Wood didn't say he was applying. The tech says he did.

panels.composition: The print shop. The TECH loading paper. WOOD leaning on the counter, casual, too casual.

balloons.text: Portland wants a portfolio. Which I'm not—

image.prompt: a print technician loading paper into a large copier while a young man leans on the counter too casually, black and white, no words
a print technician's face bent over a paper tray, not looking up, black and white, no words

balloons.text: I didn't say I was applying.

image.prompt: a young man at a counter, caught, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The copier's light sweeping. Wood with the two drawings in a folder he didn't mention bringing. The tech's hand out for them.

image.prompt: a young man handing a thin folder across a print shop counter to a technician's outstretched hand as a copier's light sweeps, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'You said Portland.' He brought the folder.
